title: Seat a PVC drain conduit in a hanger trench and set both offset retaining clips
instruction: Seat the white PVC drain conduit flush in the hanger trench, then lay each orange retaining clip flat across the conduit edge into its offset hanger slot, at least 18 mm onto the conduit.
context: Securing drain conduits and raceways into staggered support hangers is core commercial plumbing and pipefitting work (plumbers, pipefitters, and steamfitters, O*NET 47-2152.00): the conduit is seated flush into its cradle trench first, and retaining keeper clips are then set across the conduit edges at longitudinally offset hanger stations. Because each keeper clip bridges the hanger plate and the conduit top face, its flat seat exists only once the conduit is seated flush. A clip placed into an empty hanger slot tips about 23.4 degrees into the trench, and a conduit left cocked on the 5 mm cradle wall tilts the clip past 3 degrees.
setup: Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and y = -0.305 (right). The hanger trench centre F is (0.250, 0.000), on the midline. Loose, rigid, matte: the drain conduit (pipe), a white PVC (sRGB 0.88, 0.90, 0.92) block 180 x 60 x 16 mm, 110 g (printed PLA), lying flat centred at (0.220, 0.320) with its long axis along y; two retaining keeper clips, orange (sRGB 0.95, 0.55, 0.10) blocks 60 x 16 x 16 mm, 10 g each (printed PLA), lying along x in their keyways on the hanger plates, clip_plus centred at (0.250, 0.103) and clip_minus at (0.250, -0.103), bottoms 16 mm above the table. Fixed, steel grey (sRGB 0.38, 0.40, 0.44), matte, 18 blocks in all, forming one hanger frame: a cradle pocket ring 5 mm tall standing on the table, two side walls 206 x 10 x 5 mm centred at (0.250, +0.038) and (0.250, -0.038) and two end walls 10 x 66 x 5 mm centred at (0.152, 0.000) and (0.348, 0.000), giving an open trench 186 x 66 mm whose floor is the table (3 mm of clearance per side around the conduit, at most about 1.9 degrees of yaw); two hanger plates 240 x 80 x 16 mm centred at (0.250, +0.083) and (0.250, -0.083), spanning 43 to 123 mm either side of the midline against the ring's outer faces, their tops 16 mm above the table and flush with a seated conduit's top; on each plate, a keyway of four ribs 10 x 4 x 10 mm (x, y, z) centred at x 0.223 and 0.277 and y 0.091 and 0.115 (mirrored for the right plate), their inner faces 20 mm apart (2 mm either side of the stowed clip), flanking the last 8 mm at each end of the clip; on the left plate, an upstream hanger slot of two ribs 4 x 10 x 10 mm centred at x 0.202 and 0.228 and y +0.061 (slot centre x = 0.215), and on the right plate, a downstream hanger slot of two ribs 4 x 10 x 10 mm centred at x 0.272 and 0.298 and y -0.061 (slot centre x = 0.285), their inner faces 22 mm apart (3 mm either side of a set clip), spanning 56 to 66 mm from the midline, tops 26 mm above the table. Nominal end state: the conduit centred on F with its long axis along x, flat on the table inside the trench ring, top flush with the hanger plates; clip_plus along y centred at (0.215, +0.036) and clip_minus along y centred at (0.285, -0.036), each spanning 6 to 66 mm from the midline: 24 mm on the conduit, 13 mm across the 3 mm gap and the 10 mm ring wall, 23 mm on the hanger plate, its outer 10 mm between the slot ribs and its outer end in line with their outer faces. To build it: print the cradle ring and both hanger plates with their ribs as one open-floored PLA frame about 240 x 246 mm (or as two halves split on the midline, each 240 x 123 mm), tape it to the table with its outline marked, and print the conduit and clips to the stated sizes and masses.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arms have withdrawn and nothing moves (in simulation: at rest, speed under 10 mm/s and spin under 0.5 rad/s), from a top photo, a straightedge, a steel rule and a phone level. Conduit seated (P): at rest with its centre within 4 mm of F in x and y, long axis within 3 degrees of x either way round, all four bottom corners within 2 mm of the table and all four top corners within 2 mm of the hanger plate tops (16 mm up), so a conduit cocked on a ring wall, proud, outside the trench or held above it fails. A clip is set in an offset hanger slot when it rests with its long axis within 10 degrees of y either way round, a face within 3 degrees of flat, its lowest corner within 2 mm of the plate tops, its centre within 4 mm of that slot's centre line across the slot (x = 0.215 for the left upstream slot, x = 0.285 for the right downstream slot), its outer end within 4 mm of the ribs' outer faces (66 mm from the midline) along the slot, and its inner end at least 18 mm inside the conduit's side edge, measured across the conduit from where the conduit actually lies. Either clip may fill either offset slot and each slot counts once. Score: 0 without P, whatever the clips do; P alone 0.4; P and one offset slot filled 0.7; P and both offset slots filled 1.0. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. Order: without a seated conduit, a clip laid in a hanger slot has its centre 7 mm past the plate edge and tips about 23.4 degrees into the empty trench; on a conduit resting 5 mm proud on the ring it tilts about 7.9 degrees; both fail the 3 degree flatness test.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lift the conduit out and lay it flat on its start mark at (0.220, 0.320), long axis along y; lay each retaining clip back in its keyway along x at (0.250, +-0.103). The hanger frame does not move; check it against its taped outline.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid box primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and matte colours; the cradle ring, hanger plates and ribs are fixed colliders standing in for one printed hanger frame. A real J-hanger strap snaps around a round PVC pipe under spring tension; here the square-bodied drain conduit seats flush in a trench and each loose retaining clip bridges the joint into an offset rib slot and holds by its weight. Earth gravity on a bench.
